candidate_ideas.statement: Assume (CE) and (N). Twisting the two-term CE resolution by O_X(2) and using R^j p_* O_X(-2)=0 on the P^2-bundle yields F=p_*(I_C(2)) and a short exact sequence 0->F->Sym^2 E->gamma_* R->0, with F of rank two and degree nine. The kernel of the restriction H^0(Sym^2 E(-6))->H^0(C, L^{tensor 2}) equals H^0(F(-6)). Writing F isomorphic to O(s) oplus O(9-s) with s<=4, one has h^0(F(-6))=4-s, so (BAL) holds if and only if that restriction map is injective. The target H^0(C, L^{tensor 2}) has dimension seven by Riemann-Roch for a degree-12 bundle with h^1=0.

On a smooth plane quintic of genus six, C is neither hyperelliptic nor trigonal, and every g^1_4 is |H-p_0| for a point p_0. Consequently L=H+p_0 has p_0 as a base point, E is isomorphic to O(2) oplus O(3) oplus O(4), the four monomials in Sym^2 E(-6) with a_i+a_j>=6 all vanish to order at least 2 at p_0, and the seven-dimensional source maps into the six-dimensional space H^0(omega_C), so h^0(F(-6))>=1 and no degree-four pencil on a smooth plane quintic has balanced CE relations bundle.

Under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), L is base-point-free: a base point p makes |D+p| a g^2_5, a further base point produces Clifford equality on a g^2_4 and hence a hyperelliptic fibre, and a base-point-free g^2_5 is birational onto a smooth plane quintic, which cannot be balanced.

Under (CE)+(N)+(BAL), L is not isomorphic to T^{tensor 2} for any base-point-free degree-three pencil T. The case h^0(4T-omega_C)=1 forces D isomorphic to 2T-A of degree 2 and, in every configuration of A relative to the trigonal map, either h^0(D)=1 or a base point of |D|. Then h^0(2D)=3 forces E isomorphic to O(3)^{oplus 3}, the restriction map becomes the multiplication Sym^2 H^0(L)->H^0(L^{tensor 2}) with image inside the five-dimensional pullback t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(4)), and h^0(F(-6))>=1. This uses no Maroni/Hirzebruch classification.

In type (i), the point-line incidence I is an irreducible P^1-bundle over C, so monodromy on the six points of a general member of |L| is transitive. After deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus over non-normal points of the plane sextic, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible of dimension two and dominant of generic degree 30 over |L|^{rs}, so monodromy is 2-transitive and hence primitive.

In type (i) and characteristic zero, a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve X_L^vee: the Wronskian of the complete base-point-free g^2_6 has degree (r+1)d+r(r+1)(g-1)=48 and is not identically zero, and reflexivity/biduality makes the Gauss map birational onto its image. Local monodromy around that branch point is a transposition, so Jordan's theorem on a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a transposition yields monodromy S_6.

In type (ii), for every reduced member l of |L|^{rs} the pullback j^*l consists of three distinct non-branch points of the bielliptic cover psi, and phi_L^*l is the disjoint union of the three fibres. This partition is independent of the line, hence monodromy-invariant, so the image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48.

In the bielliptic-composed construction, after matching q_*O_Y=O oplus O(-2) and q_*M=O(1) oplus O(2) against gamma_* omega_C=O(-2) oplus E(-2), one obtains E isomorphic to O(2)^+ oplus O(3)^- oplus O(4)^-. The odd summand of the restriction map sends x_2 x_4 to a nonzero multiple of the unique section mu of M tensor P^{-2}. Injectivity of the even map Phi:(a,c_1,c_2)|->a nu^2 + q^*(c_1) nu mu + q^*(c_2) mu^2 follows from a pole/trace argument: f=nu/mu is a rational section of P with a single simple pole at the unique point y_0, hence is not iota-invariant when y_0 is unramified for q; a=0 would make f a pullback, while a!=0 produces a quadratic for F=f/tau over q^*k(P^1) whose trace has a simple pole at q(y_0) while c_1/(a c) is regular there. Combined with the injectivity criterion this yields F isomorphic to O(4) oplus O(5).

Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero carrying a genus-six degree-four family that is (CE)+(BAL)+(N) on every geometric fibre, AJ=P_S(pi_* L), U the reduced-support open, and Z=Ord(U) the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. If S_alpha is a connected component over which some geometric fibre is of type (i), then functoriality of pi_1^{et} along the closed fibre U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha=S_6, so Z_alpha is connected; if U_alpha is additionally normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the induction functor Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} is the identity. No irreducibility hypothesis on S is required.

Elementary numerology of the setup: chi(gamma_* O_C)=1-g=-5 and rk(gamma_* O_C)=4 give deg E=9; under (N) one has R=O_X(2)|_C of degree 36; deg W_5=16, deg W_4=20, deg L=6; and L^{tensor 2} has degree 12>2g-2 so h^1(L^{tensor 2})=0 and h^0(L^{tensor 2})=7.

established_facts.statement: For i=1,2, set W_{f_i}=O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f_i). Then deg(W_{f_i}|_C)=2(2g-2+8)-4f_i=4g+12-4f_i, the group H^0(C, omega_C tensor W^vee(Gamma)) splits as the corresponding direct sum, and that summand vanishes whenever 0>4f_i+n-2g-14.

The CE line-bundle convention is W_5:=(O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C, the f_2=5 summand of (O(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee)|_C, not the O_{P^1}(5) summand of F. For g=6 one has deg(W_5)=16 and deg(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1})=6.

On any smooth genus-6 degree-four cover C->P^1 with balanced splitting F=O(4) oplus O(5), the f=4 CE obstruction bundle omega_C tensor W_4^vee(Gamma) has degree -4 for every degree-six divisor Gamma, hence has vanishing H^0; the f=5 component has degree 0, and evaluation is obstructed on Gamma if and only if O_C(Gamma) is isomorphic to L=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}.

established_facts.statement: Granting the weak relative-canonical normalization O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_{C/P^1} tensor gamma^*A for some A in Pic(P^1), the SRC-0004 degree comparison deg(O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C)=2g+6 forces deg A=0 and A isomorphic to O_{P^1}. Hence W_5 is isomorphic to omega_C^2(-D), L is isomorphic to omega_C(-D), and M:=omega_C^2 tensor W_5^vee is isomorphic to O_C(D).
If C is hyperelliptic of genus 6 and gamma has degree 4, then necessarily gamma=q o h, E=O(1) oplus O(4) oplus O(4), and the relations bundle is exactly F=O(2) oplus O(7).
Under the fibrewise-balanced hypothesis F_b isomorphic to O(4) oplus O(5), the jump stratum B_4={h^0(L)=4} is empty, so h^0(L) is identically 3.

Under (CE)+(BAL)+(N) at (g,n)=(6,6), every geometric fibre has h^0(O_C(D))=2, h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2. Constancy uses exclusion of the hyperelliptic-composed pencil and is not equivalent to exclusion of every non-primitive degree-four pencil through a positive-genus intermediate curve.

A base point of L=omega_C(-D) would give a g^2_5, forcing the smooth-plane-quintic case. The associated tetragonal pencil is projection from that base point and has unbalanced CE relations splitting, so it is excluded from the balanced locus.

On a balanced fibre satisfying the weak CE normalization, h^0(L)=3 together with base-point-freeness of L makes the general member of |L| isomorphic to P^2 consist of six distinct points, so the reduced-support open of the closed Abel-Jacobi incidence is nonempty and dense in every fibre of the P^2-bundle.

Let U be a connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over a field and Z->U a finite etale right S_6-torsor. Connected components of Z are indexed by the orbit set H\S_6 of left multiplication (the right cosets Hg), the right deck action is transitive, and the stabilizer of Hg is g^{-1}Hg. If U is normal, integral and locally Noetherian, those components are the irreducible components, each of degree |H| over U.

Over a normal finite-type scheme base in characteristic zero, for the finite etale right S_6-torsor Z_alpha->U_alpha with monodromy image H_alpha, any additive S_6-equivariant functor F to Q-vector spaces or mixed Hodge structures satisfies F(Z_alpha) isomorphic to Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} F(Z_alpha^1) and F(Z_alpha)^{S_6} isomorphic to F(U_alpha). The isomorphism is formal and does not force Tate type.
That S_6 has rational irreducible representations does not imply that an S_6-cover of a relative configuration or linear-system space carries only Tate local systems.

established_facts.statement: For every finite flat Gorenstein cover of degree d>=3, Casnati-Ekedahl 1996 Theorem 2.1 supplies the relative-canonical embedding and the Casnati-Ekedahl resolution (two-term for d=4). SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 records O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*omega_{P^1}^vee, i.e. the strong form of (N) with trivial residual twist.

Assume (CE)+(N)+(BAL) on a smooth connected genus-6 geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with D=gamma^*O_{P^1}(1) and L=omega_C(-D) of degree 6 and h^0(L)=3, and with L base-point-free. Then phi_L:C->P^2 is finite onto an integral nondegenerate plane curve X_L with deg(phi_L)*deg(X_L)=6, and exactly one of two exclusive cases occurs: type (i), deg phi_L=1 and X_L is an integral plane sextic of geometric genus six (arithmetic genus ten, total delta invariant four) with normalization C; or type (ii), deg phi_L=2, X_L is a smooth plane cubic Y, psi=phi_L is a bielliptic double cover with psi_*O_C=O_Y oplus M^{-1} for M in Pic^5(Y), omega_C isomorphic to psi^*M, L isomorphic to psi^*N with N=O_{P^2}(1)|_Y, D isomorphic to psi^*P for P=M tensor N^{-1} in Pic^2(Y), gamma=q o psi with q=phi_{|P|} of degree two, and E isomorphic to O(2) oplus O(3) oplus O(4). Degrees 3 and 6, a singular cubic image, a hyperelliptic fibre, a smooth plane quintic, and L isomorphic to T^{tensor 2} for a base-point-free g^1_3 are excluded.

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, Y a smooth genus-one curve, P in Pic^2(Y), q=phi_{|P|}:Y->P^1, M in Pic^5(Y), B a reduced divisor in |M^{tensor 2}|, and psi:C->Y the double cover with psi_*O_C isomorphic to O_Y oplus M^{-1}. Then C is smooth and connected of genus six, gamma=q o psi is finite flat Gorenstein of degree four, and the Casnati-Ekedahl bundles split as E isomorphic to O(2) oplus O(3) oplus O(4) and F isomorphic to O(4) oplus O(5). Thus a non-primitive tetragonal pencil factoring through a genus-one curve can lie in the balanced F-locus, so primitivity is not a property of that locus. The statement addresses intermediate genus one only.

On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre satisfying (CE)+(N)+(BAL) at (g,n)=(6,6) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6, so the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected. Over any connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, H_alpha=S_6 and Z_alpha is connected; if U_alpha is additionally normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible and Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} is the identity. In type (ii) the monodromy image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6.

The forgetful map from the relative ordered distinct configuration stack Conf_6(C/B^{bal}) to the relative effective-divisor space of degree six is a finite etale S_6-torsor over the reduced-support open locus. With Q-coefficients, S_6-invariants and S_6-coinvariants agree.

On any smooth genus-6 geometric fibre of the balanced tetragonal CE family, h^0(L)=1+h^0(M) where M:=omega_C^2 tensor W_5^vee has deg M=4. Thus the h^0(L) stratification of the relative degree-six linear system is a g^1_4-type Brill-Noether question in degree 4, and h^0(L)=3 (fibrewise |L| isomorphic to P^2) precisely where h^0(M)=2. Moreover M is always special, Clifford gives h^0(M)<=3, so h^0(L) lies in {1,2,3,4} and never equals 5.

established_facts.statement: For d=3g-3+n the open input is W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{g,n}), identified by Poincare duality with W_{2d-16} H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n})(d). At (g,n)=(6,6) one has d=21, so the exact group is W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), and a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.

invalid_steps.mathematical_reason: Transitivity of G on six letters means G acts transitively on the standard set {1,...,6}, which already holds for A_6. For a right S_6-torsor the connected components are indexed by the orbit set H\S_6 of left multiplication, so connectedness is equivalent to H=S_6 (a single right coset), not to transitivity. Since [S_6:A_6]=2, an A_6 image would give two connected components.
invalid_steps.statement: Connectedness of the finite etale right S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs})->|L|^{rs} is equivalent to transitivity of the monodromy image G on the six points of a general divisor.

invalid_steps.mathematical_reason: The orbits of left multiplication of H on G are the right cosets Hg; the set of those orbits is H\G. Genuine left cosets are gH, and right multiplication on G/H={gH} is well-defined if and only if H is normal in G. The stabilizer of the component indexed by Hg is g^{-1}Hg, not gHg^{-1}, unless H is normal.
invalid_steps.statement: The set of orbits of left multiplication by a monodromy image H on S_6 may be named 'left cosets H\S_6', and the right deck action may then be written on symbols gH with component stabilizer gHg^{-1}.

unresolved_dependencies.statement: The exact monodromy image inside the wreath product S_2 wr S_3 on a type-(ii) fibre, and therefore the S_6-isotypic decomposition of cohomology of the ordering cover on a purely type-(ii) component.
Whether a connected component of a balanced+(CE)+(N) base can consist entirely of type-(ii) fibres, equivalently whether the type-(i) hypothesis in the family monodromy statement is automatic.
Whether a non-primitive degree-four pencil factoring through an intermediate curve of genus two or three can satisfy (BAL); if such a cover is balanced, degree reasons force it to be of type (i).

Extension of the family, Abel-Jacobi, and ordering-torsor statements from reduced locally Noetherian schemes to algebraic stacks with inertia (or to a smooth atlas with descent of the identification AJ=P(pi_* L)) and to nonreduced bases, where Grauert local freeness and constant-rank cohomology need a separate lifting argument.

The H_alpha-object given by ordinary or Borel-Moore cohomology of a connected component of the ordering cover, as a mixed Hodge structure; the induction isomorphism does not determine Tate type of that object.

A stack-level identification of Aut groups for the Abel-Jacobi incidence versus Aut(C,gamma,Gamma), and the existence, representability, unramifiedness, quasi-finiteness, and image-closure properties of a morphism from the balanced ordered model to M_{6,6}.

Characteristic-zero reflexivity/biduality for a reduced irreducible plane curve (birationality of the Gauss map onto the dual curve) and Jordan's theorem that a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a transposition is S_n, if these are used as inputs rather than independently established.
